objective: Keep public guest-feed posts visible to newly signed-in users who have no follows, without suppressing older public posts based on account age.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: USERS-007 is merged and deployed. Reproduce and trace the difference between the signed-out guest feed, an existing account's feed, and a newly created signed-in account with no follows before implementation; report the actual root cause in the PR.

When public posts visible on the signed-out guest feed exist, a newly signed-in account with no follows sees those same eligible public posts in its home feed, subject to the same visibility and ordering rules. Account creation time alone never excludes a public post.

A newly signed-in account's own public post appears in that account's feed and in the signed-out guest feed. Existing signed-in accounts continue to see eligible public posts from other accounts under the established feed behavior.
Tests pin old public posts, a new account with no follows, and a post authored by that new account. Tests also pin that visibility/deactivated-account rules and stable pagination are not weakened.

Do not manufacture feed items for a truly empty public dataset. The empty state is shown only when there are no eligible posts; it must not be caused solely by the viewer having no follows or being a new account.
Respect the module boundary: feed reads posts only through the posts module's public interface; it does not reach into posts' concrete classes or tables.

Browser rows on localhost, reported with evidence or NOT DONE: guest feed with existing public posts; new signed-in account with no follows sees those posts; newly authored public post is visible to its author and the guest feed; pagination remains ordered.
No new dependency or migration unless the reproduced root cause proves one necessary; if a migration is needed, make its deploy and post-deploy migration gate explicit in the PR.
wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x03-posts.md, 0x06-feed.md and 0x08-frontend.md record any changed feed contract.
